title: Post-Independence India: The Republic's Journey Since 1947

questions.question: The integration of over 560 princely states into the Indian Union was chiefly the work of:
options: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel with V. P. Menon
questions.rationale: Patel, as Home Minister (with secretary V. P. Menon), negotiated accession of almost all states — Hyderabad and Junagadh included — in 1947–48.

questions.question: The Constitution of India came into force on:
questions.rationale: Adopted 26 November 1949, it came into force 26 January 1950 — chosen to honour Purna Swaraj Day (1930).

questions.question: The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 redrew state boundaries primarily on the basis of:
questions.rationale: After Potti Sriramulu's fast created Andhra State (1953), the States Reorganisation Act and the 7th Amendment made language the basis of the map, effective 1 November 1956.

questions.question: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956) is associated with:
options: The Mahalanobis model emphasising heavy industry
questions.rationale: P. C. Mahalanobis's strategy channelled investment into capital goods and heavy industry — the steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur.

questions.question: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally launched in 1961 by Nehru together with:
questions.rationale: The Belgrade conference (1961) of Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno, and Nkrumah formalised NAM — steering clear of both Cold War blocs.

questions.question: Which pairing of year and event is correct?
questions.rationale: 1971 brought the Bangladesh war and Pakistan's surrender in Dhaka; 1962 was the China war, 1965 the second Pakistan war, and the Emergency came in 1975.

questions.question: Pokhran-I, India's first nuclear test (1974), was codenamed:
questions.rationale: 'Smiling Buddha' (18 May 1974) made India a nuclear-capable state; Pokhran-II of May 1998 (Operation Shakti) made it a declared nuclear power.

questions.question: Operation Flood, making India the world's largest milk producer, is identified with:
questions.rationale: Verghese Kurien built the Anand cooperative (Amul) into Operation Flood's national dairy grid; Swaminathan and Borlaug belong to the green revolution, Pitroda to telecom.

questions.question: The 1991 economic liberalisation was steered by:
options: Indira Gandhi and P. C. Mahalanobis
P. V. Narasimha Rao and Manmohan Singh
Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Jaswant Singh
questions.rationale: Facing a reserves crisis, PM Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh devalued the rupee, delicensed industry, and opened trade — ending the Licence Raj.

questions.question: The Kargil War (Operation Vijay), fought along the LoC, took place in:
questions.rationale: Pakistani intrusions in Kargil (summer 1999) were evicted by Indian forces — commemorated as Kargil Vijay Diwas (26 July).
